problem: A particle starts moving from the point with position vector $(-i+2j)\,\text{km},$ with an acceleration of $(i-j)\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $3j\,\text{km/h}.$ Find the distance from the particle to the origin after $4$ hours.

feedback.problem:
A weather balloon drifts from the point with position vector $(6i-j)\,\text{mi}$ and moves with a constant velocity of $(-3i+2j)\,\text{mi/h}.$ Determine the distance $(|r|)$ from the balloon to the origin after $3$ hours.

$\,|r|=$
{{field-1}}
$\text{mi}$
feedback.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant velocity $u,$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut,
$$

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=6i-j,\,u=-3i+2j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the balloon after $t=3\,\text{h}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & ={r}_{0}+ut \\  & =(6i-j)+(-3i+2j)(3) \\  & =(6i-j)+(-9i+6j) \\  & =(-3i+5j)\,\text{mi}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance from the balloon to the origin at this time is

$$
\begin{aligned}|r| & =|-3i+5j| \\  & =\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+{5}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9+25} \\  & =\sqrt{34} \\  & =\sqrt{34}\,\text{mi}.\end{aligned}
$$
